groups.high: Background location access enables an app to obtain location when the user is not actively using its interface, subject to operating-system permissions and restrictions. GPS uses satellite signals, while Wi-Fi positioning can use information about nearby access points; mobile systems may combine multiple sources. Background access is not a universal five-minute snapshot scheme, and background transmission is not necessarily postponed until the app returns to the foreground. Actual frequency, precision, storage, and upload behavior depend on the app, permissions, device, and operating system. Google Play treats background location as sensitive access and requires eligible apps to justify it, provide appropriate prominent disclosure and consent, and satisfy its permission rules. On relevant Android versions, ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION is distinct from foreground location permissions; approximate location and while-in-use access should not be confused with permission for unrestricted background tracking. A store's data disclosure and an app's privacy notice serve different roles from the device's permission settings. Location histories can reveal routes, routines, and visits to sensitive places even without recording what happened there. Conversely, permission to access location does not establish that every app continuously records an exact route or uses the same server-side reconstruction method. Check the particular Amazon app or other service's notice rather than treating a generic app-store disclosure as its full policy. Review location permission, background access, precision, stated purpose, and sharing or retention information. Disabling a permission can limit subsequent access, but it does not itself establish deletion of data already collected.
groups.mid: Background location means an app can get your location when you are not using its screen. Your phone's permissions and system rules still apply. GPS uses satellite signals. Wi-Fi positioning can use nearby access points. A phone may combine these sources. Not every app takes a reading every five minutes. An app also does not always have to wait until you open it again before sending data. Timing, accuracy, storage, and uploads depend on the app, device, permissions, and operating system. Google Play treats background location as sensitive access. An app must explain why it needs access. It must tell you clearly what it does. It must meet rules about consent and access. Consent means saying yes. Some Android versions have a separate background permission. Its name is ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION. Approximate location means a less exact position. While-in-use access is not a right to track you all the time. An app-store notice, the app's privacy notice, and phone permissions do different jobs. Location history can show routes, routines, and visits to sensitive places. It does not prove what you did there. Nor does access prove every app records your exact route all the time. Check the notice for the actual Amazon app or other service. Check if access runs in the background. Check how exact it is and why it is used. Check who gets the data. Check retention too. Retention means how long data is kept. Turning a permission off can limit future access. It does not automatically delete data already collected.
groups.low: An app may get your location even when you are not using its screen. This is background location access. Your phone still has rules. Its access settings still apply. GPS uses signals from satellites. Wi-Fi can help work out where you are by using nearby access points. A phone may use both. Not every app checks every five minutes. Not every app waits until you open it again to send data. How often it checks, how exact the result is, and what it sends depend on the app and phone. Google Play treats this access as sensitive. An app must meet rules about why it needs access, how it tells you, consent, and permissions. Consent means saying yes. On relevant Android versions, ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION is the name of a separate background permission. Approximate location means a less exact location. While-in-use access is not the same as unlimited background access. The app-store notice, the app's privacy notice, and your phone settings do different jobs. Location history may show routes, routines, or visits to private places. It does not prove what you did there. And access does not prove every app records your exact route all the time. Read the notice for the Amazon app or other service you actually use. Check background access, accuracy, purpose, sharing, and how long data is kept. Turning access off can limit future use. It does not by itself delete data already collected.
groups.source_review: Official Google Play background-location and sensitive-permission guidance checked. Amazon's general notice was unavailable; no specific Amazon app behavior asserted without its notice.
groups.notes: Removed fabricated universal five-minute sampling, foreground-only upload and all-app Wi-Fi/GPS architecture claims. Preserved purpose, precision and privacy distinctions.

groups.high: Know Your Customer (KYC) and Customer Due Diligence (CDD) records help a mobile financial services provider establish customer identity, monitor transactions, and support regulatory or law-enforcement review. Bangladesh Bank's Mobile Financial Services Regulations, 2018, Section 18.1, required KYC and CDD records for mobile-account holders and wholesale and retail agents, together with MFS transaction records, to be retained for not less than six years from their dates of origination. The records had to be readily reproducible for later reference by the provider or relevant authorities. Section 18.2 also addressed providing copies or printouts of relevant transaction records on request within the prescribed preservation period. This is a minimum measured from origination, not a general five-to-ten-year period beginning at account closure. A National Identity Card (NID) and, where applicable identity-verification rules require it, biometric verification may contribute to checking identity. That does not establish that every provider keeps every customer's raw biometric template or that verification eliminates fraud. The 2018 text should not be treated as proof of a particular AES-256, multi-factor-authentication, or database architecture in every deployment. Retaining identity information creates security and access-control responsibilities, not permission for unlimited unrelated use. A lost phone does not necessarily erase provider-held records, while account closure does not automatically override a lawful retention duty. This explanation concerns the specified 2018 instrument; later Bangladesh Bank regulations and identity-verification directions must be checked for current requirements.
groups.mid: KYC means Know Your Customer, while CDD means Customer Due Diligence. These records help a mobile money firm check who you are. They help it check transactions. They help it answer lawful inquiries. The rule is in Section 18.1. It comes from Bangladesh Bank's Mobile Financial Services Regulations, 2018. KYC and CDD records had to be kept for mobile-account holders and wholesale and retail agents. MFS transaction records had to be kept too. The minimum was six years from their dates of origination. That means when the records began, not automatically when an account closed. The firm had to be able to reproduce them for later use by itself or the relevant authorities. In other words, copies had to be available. Section 18.2 also covered copies or printouts of relevant transaction records on request during the required storage period. An NID is a National Identity Card. It can help verify identity. Biometric checks may also apply under the relevant identity rules. But that does not prove every provider stores each person's raw fingerprint template. It does not stop all fraud. The 2018 text is not proof that every firm uses the same AES-256 encryption or login system. Kept records still need protection against unauthorized access. Keeping data does not permit any unrelated use. A lost phone does not necessarily erase the firm's records. Closing an account does not automatically end a lawful retention duty. Retention means keeping records. This describes the 2018 instrument. Later rules matter too. Check later regulations and directions on how to check identity for the rules now in force.
groups.low: A mobile money provider needs to check who its customers are. KYC means Know Your Customer. CDD means Customer Due Diligence. These records help with identity checks, transaction checks, and lawful inquiries. Bangladesh Bank issued Mobile Financial Services Regulations, 2018. Section 18.1 gave a rule for keeping records. KYC and CDD records had to be kept. This covered mobile-account holders and wholesale and retail agents. MFS transaction records had to be kept too. The minimum was six years from the dates they began. It was not simply six years from account closure. The provider had to be able to reproduce them for later use by itself or the relevant authorities. Section 18.2 also covered giving copies or printouts of relevant transaction records on request during the required storage period. Your NID is your National Identity Card. It can help check who you are. Biometric checks, such as checks involving fingerprints, may also apply under the rules. But that does not prove every firm keeps every raw fingerprint template. It does not make all fraud impossible. The 2018 rules do not prove that every firm uses the same AES-256 encryption or login system. A firm still has to protect access to kept records. Keeping them does not allow any unrelated use it likes. Losing a phone does not necessarily erase the firm's records. Closing an account does not automatically end a lawful duty to keep data. This explains the 2018 instrument. Later regulations and identity-check directions matter to the rules now in force.
groups.source_review: Official 2018 Section 18.1–18.2 checked; minimum six years from origination verified. Later 2022 instrument identified; no claim that 2018 alone states all current requirements.
groups.notes: Replaced invented 5–10 years after termination with the actual six-year origination rule. Removed universal raw-biometric and deployment-specific security guarantees.

groups.high: Automated website crawling is software-based retrieval and examination of web pages. It can support fraud monitoring by comparing publicly displayed merchant activity with information supplied to a payment provider, but it is not synonymous with anti-money-laundering compliance. PayPal's Acceptable Use Policy prohibits specified activities and transactions; its existence does not establish a universal legal mandate to crawl the dark web or a particular detection architecture. Reviewing a merchant's website may help identify prohibited products, misleading descriptions, or inconsistencies requiring further review. A website signal is evidence to assess, not proof of money laundering, dishonest intent, or beneficial ownership. Nor does it replace customer verification, transaction monitoring, investigation, or applicable reporting obligations. Natural Language Processing (NLP), entity resolution, and graph analysis are examples of analytical methods, not confirmed PayPal implementations merely because they could be used. References to FATF, politically exposed persons (PEPs), or Tornado Cash do not by themselves show that the policy requires a named tool, screening system, or cryptocurrency investigation. Collection must also respect applicable law and access restrictions; a security purpose does not grant unrestricted permission to obtain private content. Businesses should understand the relevant Acceptable Use Policy edition, ensure accurate merchant information, and respond to legitimate compliance inquiries. The important distinction is between an illustrative monitoring technique, PayPal's actual contractual restrictions, and legal duties established by the competent regulator.
groups.mid: Automated website crawling means software visits and checks web pages. It can help a payment firm compare what a merchant sells online with the information it supplied. That may reveal banned products, misleading claims, or details that need checking. It is not proof of money laundering. Money laundering means making money from crime look lawful. PayPal's Acceptable Use Policy bans specified activities and transactions. The policy does not prove every provider must crawl the dark web or use a named fraud system. Firms may also need customer checks, transaction monitoring, inquiries, and reports required by law. Crawling does not replace that work. Some possible methods have technical names. Natural Language Processing, or NLP, analyzes text. Entity resolution links names that refer to the same person or company. Graph analysis studies links between them. These are possible methods, not confirmed PayPal systems. The same warning applies to names such as FATF, politically exposed persons or PEPs, and Tornado Cash. A name does not establish that the policy requires a particular tool or cryptocurrency inquiry. A suspicious page is a reason to check further. It is not proof of intent or who owns a business. Data collection still has to respect the law and access limits. A fraud-prevention purpose does not permit unlimited access to private content. A business should check the policy that applies, give accurate information about its work, and answer legitimate compliance questions. Keep possible methods, actual contract terms, and legal duties separate.
groups.low: Website crawling means software visits and checks web pages. A payment firm could use it to compare a shop's website with what the shop said it sells. It might find banned goods, misleading claims, or details that need checking. That is not proof of money laundering. Money laundering means making money from crime look lawful. PayPal's Acceptable Use Policy bans certain activities and transactions. That does not prove every firm must check the dark web or use one named fraud tool. Firms may also need identity checks, transaction checks, inquiries, and reports required by law. Crawling does not replace that work. Some tools have long names. Natural Language Processing, or NLP, checks text. Entity resolution links names that refer to the same person or firm. Graph analysis looks at links between them. These are possible tools. They are not proof of what PayPal uses. You may see names such as FATF, PEPs, and Tornado Cash. They do not prove the policy requires one tool. PEPs means politically exposed persons. A name alone does not prove a required crypto inquiry either. A suspicious page is a clue to check, not proof of someone's intent or who owns a firm. Collection still has to fit the law and access limits. A safety purpose does not give a firm free access to private content. A business should read the policy that applies, give true details about its work, and answer legitimate compliance questions. Do not mix up possible methods, actual contract terms, and legal duties.
groups.source_review: Official acceptable-use policy and user agreement opened. A requirement for the original dark-web/NLP/graph/Tornado-Cash architecture was not established; such methods are explicitly illustrative, not attributed as mandates.
groups.notes: Corrected unsupported implementation and universal regulatory-mandate claims. Technical terms retained only as clearly qualified concepts, not as evidence of PayPal deployment.

groups.high: A training opt-out concerns whether eligible content is used to develop or improve models; it is not identical to deleting stored conversations or exercising every statutory privacy right. In consumer services where improvement use applies, the relevant account's data controls and service terms determine the available choice and scope. Verify the setting for the actual product rather than assuming one universal policy. OpenAI's official API documentation states that, from 1 March 2023, data sent to the API is not used to train or improve its models unless the customer explicitly opts in. API usage therefore must not be described as automatically consenting to training by default. OpenAI also distinguishes training use from abuse-monitoring logs and application state. A service can retain some content for permitted operational or safety purposes without using it for model training; retention depends on the endpoint, feature, applicable requirements, and approved controls. Opting out of future training use does not establish immediate deletion of every copy or removal of an earlier contribution from existing model weights. Conversely, the documentation does not justify claiming that each opt-out triggers retraining, introduces backdoors, or has a particular implementation delay. To make an informed choice, identify the product and account type, review its training-sharing control and scope, and consider deletion or retention questions separately. Avoid submitting unnecessary sensitive information merely because a training opt-out or no-training default applies.
groups.mid: A training opt-out is a choice about using eligible content to improve AI models. It is not the same as deleting a chat or exercising every privacy right. For a consumer service where improvement use applies, check the product's terms and your account's data controls. OpenAI products do not all have the same rule. The API is an important example. OpenAI says data sent to the API has not been used for training by default since 1 March 2023. That use needs an explicit opt-in. Using the API is not automatic training permission. Does no training mean no storage? No. OpenAI describes abuse-monitoring logs and application state. Logs help deal with misuse. Application state is data a feature keeps to do its task. Some content may stay for allowed safety or service purposes without being used for training. The endpoint, feature, law, and approved controls matter. An endpoint is the part of the API you use. Stopping future training use does not prove every stored copy has been deleted. It also does not promise removal of earlier use from an existing model. But do not assume an opt-out causes retraining, security backdoors, or a fixed delay either. The documentation does not establish those claims. Check the product, account type, and scope of the training-sharing choice. Check deletion on its own. Check retention too. Retention means keeping data. Even with an opt-out or no-training default, avoid sending private details that are not needed.
groups.low: An AI training opt-out lets you choose not to have eligible content used to improve models. That is not the same as deleting a chat. It does not cover every privacy right either. For a consumer service where this use applies, check its terms and your account's data controls. Different OpenAI products can have different rules. The API is one important example. OpenAI says data sent to the API has not been used for training by default since 1 March 2023. You must explicitly opt in for that use. Just using the API does not give training permission. Does no training mean nothing is stored? No. OpenAI describes abuse-monitoring logs and application state. Logs help deal with misuse. Application state means data a feature keeps to do its task. Some content may stay for allowed safety or service purposes without being used for training. The feature, endpoint, law, and approved controls matter. An endpoint is the part of the API you use. Stopping future training use does not prove every stored copy is gone. It does not promise to remove earlier use from a model that already exists. But it does not prove an opt-out causes retraining, backdoors, or a fixed delay. Those claims are not established by the documentation. Check your product, account, and training-sharing choice. Read what the deletion and retention rules cover too. Retention means keeping data. Even with no training use, do not send private details that are not needed.
groups.source_review: Official API data-controls documentation and ChatGPT controls page fetched. API no-training default verified. Consumer controls kept product/account-conditional; no unsupported current UI or universal consumer default asserted.
groups.notes: Corrected automatic API-training claim and invented opt-out retraining/backdoor/latency mechanism. Distinguished training permission from retention, deletion and historical model contributions.
